title: bug: qa_reject's failedDodItems entries have no type or length check (only the 20-item count is capped), so a numeric DoD index throws an uncoded "s.trim is not a function" and a 100k-char entry is stored, while qa_reject bounds reason and issues and submit_plan_critique bounds its concerns
description:
Held item (b) from hunt #10 (task-49a2c07f, architect-1dd28c7c, msg-e3e8725e), filed by the governor. Re-checked at tip 8ca8d389: qaReject.ts is unchanged since the hunt's repro HEAD 677d051a. No stored entry is affected yet (0 of 101 real failedDodItems entries are non-strings or oversized), hence LOW.

PROBLEM. qa_reject validates the count of failedDodItems but not the entries. A non-string entry, such as a DoD index sent as a number, crashes the handler with an uncoded TypeError instead of a coded INVALID_INPUT. An entry of any length is stored in rejectionDetails and carried into the repeated-failure tracking. Its sibling fields are bounded: reason has MAX_REASON_LENGTH, and issues[].description is refused over 500 chars.

EVIDENCE (at 8ca8d389):
- qaReject.ts:87-88 caps the count (`> 20` → invalidInput). qaReject.ts:141 maps `(s) => s.trim()` over every entry with no typeof check and no length bound, and :150 stores the result in rejectionDetails.failedDodItems.
- The siblings bound their text: qaReject.ts:82-83 (reason) and :103-104 (issues.description, 500). submitPlanCritique.ts:8-9 (MAX_CONCERNS 20, MAX_CONCERN_LEN 1000) with its array type check at :67-68.
- Repro: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-49a2c07f/B/zzHuntB_failedDodItems.test.ts, output B/B_failedDodItems.out.txt at 677d051a: "Tests 2 failed | 1 passed (3)". A numeric entry gives "TypeError: s.trim is not a function", where `{ code: -32602 }` was expected. An over-long entry is stored: "expected [ Array(3) ] to deeply equal []".

FIX DIRECTION. Before any write, refuse a non-string entry and an entry over a bound with a coded INVALID_INPUT. That matches qa_reject's own refusals for reason and issues. Use the DoD-item length (1000) or submit_plan_critique's MAX_CONCERN_LEN as the bound. Refusal (not truncation) keeps the repeated-failure matching exact.

PLACEMENT. No open row edits qaReject.ts. No dependsOn.
definitionOfDone: qa_reject refuses a failedDodItems entry that is not a string with a coded INVALID_INPUT (no uncoded TypeError), and writes nothing.

qa_reject refuses (coded INVALID_INPUT, nothing written) a failedDodItems entry longer than the chosen bound (at most 1000 chars), so no stored rejectionDetails entry exceeds it. Valid rejections, including the repeated-failure escalation, behave as before.

The hunt repro (zzHuntB_failedDodItems.test.ts) ported into the package's qa_reject tests passes 3 of 3, where it gave 2 failed | 1 passed at 677d051a, and the existing qa_reject test files stay green in a snapshot outside the shared checkout.

implementationPlan.note: Self-review: (a) the validation block is synchronous and sits before getTask, assertWorkerOwns, assertReviewBinding and every write; (r3)-(r5) pin the bytes on disk. (b) The bound uses the trimmed length, which is what is stored; (c2) at 1000 and (r5) at 1001 bracket it. (c) null/undefined/[] skip the block, and dedupe and the repeat-failure flips are untouched (qaOwnership and qaReject suites green). (d) The error text names failedDodItems[i]. (e) git status lists only the two planned files. (f) No forbidden pattern in the diff. Theoretical: an array with holes (sparse) skips forEach holes, then the later .map(trim) would hit undefined, but JSON args cannot carry sparse arrays.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: moe.qa_reject validates failedDodItems as an array of at most 20 strings, each at most 1000 chars after trimming (the stored DoD-item bound), before any lookup or write. A non-array value, a non-string entry, or an over-long entry is refused with a coded INVALID_INPUT naming the field index, and nothing is written. Valid rejections behave exactly as before.
invariants: A refused qa_reject writes nothing: no task write, no review record, no activity event, no chat line.
The 'too many items (max 20)' refusal keeps its text. Entries are refused, never truncated, so repeated-failure matching stays exact.
null, undefined and [] still mean no failed items, and duplicates are still deduped within one reject.
compatibility: qaReject.test.ts, qaOwnership.test.ts, qaApprove.test.ts and the other listed suites pass unchanged.
The qa_reject inputSchema and response shapes are unchanged. docs/MCP_SERVER.md is not edited (held by another row); its `failedDodItems?: string[], // max 20` line stays true.
reuse: invalidInput from util/errors.js, the code every other qa_reject refusal uses.
The hunt repro's fixture and three cases, ported verbatim as (c1), (r1) and (r2).
sourceAssumptions: tools/qaReject.ts:86-89 checks only `params.failedDodItems.length > 20`. :140-142 dedupes with `.map((s) => s.trim())`, which throws a TypeError on a non-string or null entry. :150 stores the result. The file is byte-identical at 677d051a and 6ded0c93.
tools/qaReject.ts:81-84 caps reason at 2000 and :103-104 caps issues[].description at 500. submitPlanCritique.ts bounds its concerns at MAX_CONCERN_LEN 1000.
state/taskStore.ts stores definitionOfDone through sanitizeStringArray(..., 50, 1000), so a DoD item is at most 1000 chars.

approachesConsidered: Truncating long entries to 1000, as submit_plan_critique does for concerns, was rejected: the DoD says refuse, and truncation would make two different over-long items compare equal in the repeated-failure log.
Measuring the raw length instead of the trimmed length was rejected, because the trimmed text is what gets stored and matched.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: qa_reject's text fields: reason is capped at 2000 and issues[].description at 500 with a non-empty check, but failedDodItems had only the count cap. Its entries feed rejectionDetails, rejectionHistory (20 entries), the 100-entry failedDodItems log and the same-item-twice PLANNING flip. None of the 101 real entries on this board is a non-string or over 536 chars.
risks: A QA seat that names DoD items by index now gets INVALID_INPUT and must resend the item text. Today the call crashes uncoded and records nothing, so this only improves that path.
